canonical_question: Does the 'small' enthalpy of mixing refer to values closer to zero (less negative) or simply lower in magnitude compared to other pairs?

answers.answer: The text mentions that the enthalpy of mixing formed between Cr and other refractory elements is small, but it does not specify the numerical range or define 'small' as being closer to zero or lower in magnitude compared to other pairs.
answers.material: RHEAs with Cr, W, V, Ta, Ti
answers.mechanism: formation of dense oxidation film or brittle intermetallics
answers.boundary_limitation: No specific values or comparative magnitude definitions for 'small' enthalpy of mixing are provided in the text.
evidence_spans: Previous studies focused on mechanical properties at high- and room-temperatures, but with little research and analysis on high-temperature oxidation resistance [ [7] , [8] , [9] ].

The research shows that adding the proper amount of Al, Cr, and Si elements into the refractory high-entropy alloy can form a dense oxidation film on the surface of the alloy in a high-temperature environment, thus improving the high-temperature oxidation resistance [ [10] , [11] , [12] , [13] ].
Unfortunately, elements Al, Cr, and Si very easily form brittle intermetallic compounds with other refractory elements, resulting in reduced mechanical properties of RHEAs [ [14] , [15] , [16] ].
